Container.Name: tordownloader
Container.Overview: TorBox as a download client for Sonarr and Radarr. tordownloader implements the qBittorrent WebUI API, sends the torrents it receives to TorBox, and downloads the finished files to your downloads share for Sonarr/Radarr to import. No mount: real files on disk.[br][br]After starting, add it in Sonarr/Radarr as a qBittorrent download client (host: this server's IP, port 6500, no username/password). Map /downloads to the same host folder Sonarr/Radarr use, at the same container path, so imports can hardlink. Set the Sonarr/Radarr URL and API key so failed downloads are blocklisted and replaced. Status page: the WebUI link.
Container.Requires: A TorBox account and API key (torbox.app). A /downloads share mapped identically in Sonarr/Radarr.

Config.Name: WebUI / API port
Config.Description: qBittorrent API used by Sonarr/Radarr, plus the status page, /healthz and /metrics.

Config.Name: Downloads
Config.Description: Where finished files are written (category subfolders inside). Must be the same host folder Sonarr/Radarr see as /downloads.

Config.Name: AppData
Config.Description: State database (tordownloader.db). Optional: put a config.yaml here (copy config.example.yaml from the repo) for settings not exposed below, such as slot count, timeouts and the free-space reserve. Restart the container after editing it.

Config.Name: TorBox API key
Config.Description: Your TorBox API key (torbox.app → Settings). Checked at startup; problems are logged.

Config.Name: Sonarr URL
Config.Description: e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8989. With the API key, failed downloads are blocklisted in Sonarr and a replacement is searched. Strongly recommended.

Config.Name: Radarr URL
Config.Description: e.g. http://192.168.1.10:7878. Same failed-download handling for Radarr.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID that owns downloaded files (99 = nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID that owns downloaded files (100 = users).

Config.Name: Database path
Config.Description: SQLite state file inside the container. Keep it under /data.
